title: Count Increasing Quadruplets
summary: Given an array nums of size n with elements from 1 to n, count the number of quadruplets (i, j, k, l) such that 0 <= i < j < k < l < n and nums[i] < nums[k] < nums[j] < nums[l].
statement: Given an array nums of size n with elements from 1 to n, count the number of quadruplets (i, j, k, l) such that 0 <= i < j < k < l < n and nums[i] < nums[k] < nums[j] < nums[l].
constraints: nums is a permutation of integers 1 through n.
Count index quadruplets i<j<k<l satisfying nums[i]<nums[k]<nums[j]<nums[l].
Return the total number of qualifying quadruplets.
hints: Fix the middle inversion j<k with nums[k]<nums[j].
Count earlier indices i with nums[i]<nums[k] and later indices l with nums[l]>nums[j].
Multiply those independent left and right counts for the fixed middle pair and sum them.
Every valid quadruplet has exactly one middle pair (j,k), so the products count all solutions once.
